text:
How do you get an AI to write a P6 schedule that P6 itself agrees with? This is the part of my system I trust most, and the reason why.

1. The schedule is a model, not a file. WBS, activities, logic, calendars and key dates sit in Python. Change one rule and the whole baseline rebuilds.

2. The model writes P6's own format. An XER is a text file of tables: PROJWBS, TASK, TASKPRED, CALENDAR, RSRC, TASKRSRC. The engine writes each one, including 21-point resource curves.

3. A second engine checks the first. A separate critical-path calculation repeats P6's rules: several calendars, lags on the predecessor's calendar, milestones that snap differently from tasks. On one schedule it matched P6 on 1,665 of 1,665 dates and floats.

4. Then the traps. These are things P6 does not warn you about, and the import check now tests for each:
• A number written in the wrong format. P6 rejects the file.
• A resource on the wrong type of calendar. P6 imports the file and silently drops the assignments.
• A date that lands on a holiday boundary.
• A reused project ID, which overwrites the live schedule on import.

The first and third were caught by the checks before a file reached me.

The result on one job: a 281-activity baseline with 167 client and contract milestones, imported as a new project, and built so that F9 in P6 moves no dates.

I still set the sequence, the tiers and the production rates. The engine makes sure P6 and I mean the same thing.

Planners: has P6 ever silently changed something on import? What was it?
